 New Proposed SNAP Change Could Cut Assistance to Millions More People
 The Trump administration has revived efforts to further restrict food aid eligibility.
 By Rebekah Alvey

 --> November 10, 2026 – The Trump administration has proposed new changes to federal food assistance programs that would cause millions of households to lose benefits.

 On Monday, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) issued a rule proposal that would restrict automatic eligibility for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) for households receiving non-cash assistance from the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families Program (TANF).
 The proposal is expected to cut nearly 18 percent of SNAP recipients, about 6.3 million people, according to the agency’s estimates. Already SNAP participation has dropped by about 5.5 million people under the Trump administration, due to changes from the Republicans’ One Big Beautiful Bill and other policy shifts.
 Currently, more than 40 states choose to offer broad-based categorical eligibility (BBCE). This allows households already receiving cash and non-cash assistance from TANF to automatically qualify for SNAP, even if they are making or have assets above the typical SNAP thresholds.
 On top of allowing more low-income families to participate, BBCE also makes SNAP administration easier for states.
 The latest USDA proposal would restrict this option and eliminate eligibility for families receiving noncash assistance like job training or child care vouchers.
 If implemented, the USDA estimates that 6.3 million fewer people would qualify for SNAP in fiscal year 2029, the first year the rule would take effect.
 The agency estimates this would cut federal and state spending on benefits by more than $50 billion over five years. But it would also increase SNAP administrative costs, by $1.24 billion, with states now expected to take up a larger share .
 In the proposal, USDA argues that BBCE has allowed families to benefit from SNAP despite exceeding income or asset thresholds.
 Crystal FitzSimons, president of the Food Research and Action Center (FRAC), called the proposal “unconscionable,” especially given the additional cuts to SNAP through the OBBB.
 BBCE has allowed individuals with net incomes below the poverty line, or with limited income, to qualify for SNAP, FitzSimons said in a statement. This helps those in areas with a higher cost of living, or working parents earning low wages, she continued.

 Sign up today Sign up today Under the proposed change 1.8 million children would no longer be automatically eligible for free school meals , according to agency estimates. Some may still qualify for free meals, but would need to go submit more paperwork, which can be onerous for schools and families.
 FRAC noted the move could also interfere with schools’ participation in the Community Eligibility Provision (CEP), which makes it easier for schools with a high population of students on SNAP or other support programs to offer free and reduced meals .
 More than 5,000 people would lose access to the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC).
 Representative Angie Craig (D-Minnesota), ranking member of the House Agriculture Committee, called the proposal  “heartless and cruel.”
 “Unfortunately, the Trump administration and the outgoing Republican majority in Congress have undermined the program’s integrity at every turn, harming millions of vulnerable Americans in the process,” Craig said in a statement.
 The proposal is now open for a 30-day comment period. ( Link to this post .)
